author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Hundreds of thousands of protesters in Spain have joined mass demonstrations in at least three cities after parliament failed Friday to pass emergency measures to address a housing affordability crisis. Rent has doubled in Spain over the past decade, with many accusing large corporations, often depicted as vultures on placards, of buying homes and charging exorbitant rents.

On average, Spain issues at least 45 eviction orders daily, but it was an 87-year-old pensioner unable to afford a 430 percent rent hike who helped ignite the mobilisation. 

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez presented an emergency package to parliament to ease the anger, but right-wing parties blocked it. Protests that began in Madrid have since spread to Barcelona and Valencia, with demonstrators demanding what they say their constitution already guarantees: the right to decent and adequate housing.

Al Jazeera's Michael Appel reports.

AI is now creating digital versions of real people that are almost impossible to distinguish from the original, promising a transformation of the media and marketing industry. 

Daniel Yap, founder of a talent agency that builds "digital twins," says the technology is improving so fast that it may be undetectable within six months. 

Malaysia's experiments with digital twinning have had setbacks. A government attempt to create an AI version of the prime minister was withdrawn after just a day to fix problems. Still, proponents argue the technology will enhance rather than replace real talent, warning that personalities who don't participate risk being left behind in a fast-growing AI economy, with Yap saying the goal is to ensure real people aren't left unrepresented.

Al Jazeera's Rob McBride reports from Kuala Lumpur.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Amid the tacos and tamales of Mexico City's street food scene, Palestinian brothers Fadi and Mohammed Abed now serve falafel and shawarma, bringing a taste of home to their new city. Fadi says Mexicans have taken to the food, even as he mourns what he left behind: a warehouse, three houses and three cars in Palestine, all gone. He arrived with nothing, but is "getting by little by little," he says.

The brothers arrived in Mexico in 2025 with their families after their father, a Mexican citizen, helped secure their evacuation from Gaza. They had no phones or money, borrowing about $50 to set up stalls now two kilometres apart. 

Al Jazeera's Cara Legg reports from Mexico City.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Joshua Kerry, the man charged with murdering Reform UK member Anne Widdecombe, has also been charged with preparing acts of terror, including against the party's leader, Nigel Farage. Counter-terrorism police say the charge relates to activity alleged to have taken place between 2024 and July this year. Kerry, 28, from Rotherham, is due in court on Wednesday over the terror charge.

Security for MPs was reassessed under Operation Bridger in 2016 following the murder of MP Jo Cox, and again after another MP was killed in 2021. Protections exist both in parliament and in MPs' local areas, but this latest threat is likely to raise fresh questions over whether they go far enough.

Al Jazeera's Camille Nedelec reports from London.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A stand-off over a contested road in Portadown, Northern Ireland, is continuing after talks between Garvaghy Road residents and the Orange Order broke down on Thursday evening. 

Residents have launched a fresh legal challenge to try to block the march from going through their community, with a court hearing originally set for Friday postponed until Monday to allow more time for a possible compromise.

The road is controversial because of its history: during Orange Order marches in the 1990s it was the scene of serious disorder that largely ended with the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. Last week, after nearly 30 years, the loyalist Orange Order, who want Northern Ireland to remain part of the UK, was given permission to march through the nationalist area, where residents want Northern Ireland to become part of the Irish Republic. 

Al Jazeera's Milena Veselinovic reports from Portadown, Northern Ireland.

description:
Jennifer Gavito, a former acting principal deputy assistant secretary of state for Near Eastern Affairs and senior advisor at the Cohen Group, responds to comments from Reserve Major General Nitzan Alon, the former head of Israel's hostage headquarters, who said Israeli captives in Gaza could have been brought home up to a year earlier, potentially saving thousands of lives on both sides.

Gavito says the claim reignites debate over whether Israel prioritised defeating Hamas over securing hostages' return, but is sceptical the thesis can be proven, given how difficult and opaque ceasefire negotiations tend to be. 

She notes the Biden administration was broadly supportive of Israel after October 7, though former Secretary of State Antony Blinken later suggested by May 2024 that Washington had concerns Israel's operational objectives had largely been met before a mediation deal was offered.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
American farmers say they are losing patience with President Donald Trump's trade war with China, as rising diesel and fertiliser costs squeeze margins and falling exports push more farms into bankruptcy. 

Nearly 70 percent of rural America voted for Trump, but his approval is now negative in nine of the country's ten biggest farm states, including Minnesota, where farmer Sam Ziegler's family has farmed since 1918. Ziegler, who voted for Trump in 2016, says he is now asking harder questions about whether the administration truly supports rural America. 

Farmers say they want trade, not aid, and open markets rather than tariffs that hit US farm sales to China.

Al Jazeera's Heidi Zhou-Castro reports from Good Thunder, Minnesota.
